subject: Pharmacology
concept: Antiparasitic therapy depends on parasite species, clinical form, geographic setting and host factors.

content.definition: Pharmacologic treatment targets the relevant parasite stage and clinical form.
content.explanation: Leishmaniasis treatment may include liposomal amphotericin B, pentavalent antimonials, miltefosine or other region-specific agents. Lymphatic filariasis control uses combinations selected according to transmission setting.
content.mechanism: Antiparasitic agents act through parasite membrane, metabolic, mitochondrial or other essential pathways depending on the drug.
content.clinical_relevance: Current recommendations differ by species and geography; WHO guidance should be checked for the exact setting.
content.treatment: Treatment should follow current WHO or national guidance and account for species, disease form, contraindications and monitoring needs.
high_yield: Leishmaniasis therapy is species- and region-dependent.
Liposomal amphotericin B is an important treatment option for visceral leishmaniasis in appropriate settings.
Filariasis treatment is linked to transmission-control strategy as well as individual infection.
Drug toxicity and interactions vary among antiparasitic agents.

yemen_context.relevance: Leishmaniasis and filarial disease are important infectious-disease pharmacology topics in the region.
yemen_context.evidence: General evidence; no Yemen-specific regimen asserted.

review_notes: Original synthesis aligned with current WHO leishmaniasis guidance and standard filariasis guidance.
